about: HCD's written findings on Anaheim's and Irvine's ADU (and Anaheim's SB 9) ordinances, as structured data. Used as an answer key to score Fast Path Check audits (web/lib/features/hcd-score.ts). Summaries are ours, paraphrased from the letters; read the letters for exact wording. HCD reviewed each city's ORDINANCE, not its checklist, so only findings whose subject appears in the document being audited are in scope for scoring.

letters.reviewed: ADU Ordinance No. 6570 (adopted 2024-03-19) and SB 9 Ordinance No. 6524 (adopted 2022-01-11)
letters.responseDue: 30 days (the letter's text says 'April 23, 2024', apparently a typo for 2025)

findings.summary: Cites 65852.2, 65852.22 and 65852.26, which SB 477 deleted; must cite Chapter 13 (66310-66342).
Limits on the number of ADUs/JADUs conflict with the units state law requires cities to allow.
Location limits on detached units go beyond what state law permits.
Sprinkler rule must reflect state limits (an ADU can't trigger sprinklers in the primary dwelling).
Uses subjective standards; only objective standards are allowed.
Historic-inventory rule goes beyond the state's historic-resource provisions.
Ban on separate sale must note the 66341 nonprofit exception; 66342 allows an optional condo-style ordinance.
Treats unpermitted existing ADUs as unlawful; state law limits denying permits for unpermitted ADUs.
Conversion rule must align with the state definition of an ADU.
Says applications not approved in 60 days are denied; a denial must come with a full written list of deficiencies and how to fix them (66317(b)).
Limits ADUs/JADUs on SB 9 lots in ways state law doesn't allow.
Same issue in the SB 9 ordinance.
Unit allowances must follow 65852.21(a).
Standards must be objective as defined in 65852.21(i)(2).
Setback rule conflicts with SB 9's limits.
SB 9 approvals must be ministerial, without discretionary hearings.
Further subjective standards that must be made objective.

followUp.summary: Irvine didn't amend Ord. 18-05 and will rely on State ADU Law directly; it may restrict separate sale of ADUs.

findings.summary: Cites 65852.2, 65852.22 and 65852.26, which SB 477 deleted.
Doesn't provide for the ADU/JADU combinations 66323(a) requires cities to approve ministerially.
Definitions (e.g. of garages and ADUs) conflict with state definitions.
Limits ADUs to lots with single-family homes; state law allows them in zones permitting single-family or multifamily use.
Requires an owner-occupant applicant and deed restrictions on all ADUs; 66315 prohibits these (except limiting rentals to 30+ days).
Allows 120 days to decide; 66317 requires 60 days from a complete application.
Requires fixing nonconforming conditions (e.g. parking) as a condition of ADU approval.
5,000 sq ft minimum lot size, size caps by lot size, and subjective design standards.
Setbacks exceed the state's 4-foot side and rear limit.
Local building standards go beyond what state law allows for ADUs.
Must state that an ADU can't trigger sprinklers in the primary dwelling (66314(d)(12)); size limits conflict with state minimums.
Height limits are below the state minimums.
Parking requirements conflict with the state's exemptions.
Separate-sale rule must reflect the state exceptions.
